You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Evidence: task-9c09985c showed an 11x13 grid split into four 5x6 panels by row 5 and column 6 (separator color 2); copied top-left pattern to all four. A 2x3 arrangement of 5x4 panels separated by color 3 copied the bottom-right panel to all six. A 5x11 grid split by columns 3 and 7 (separator color 7) copied a left 5x3 pattern [[8,5,5],[5,8,5],[5,5,5],[5,9,3],[1,1,5]] into the other panels. Newly confirmed with 0 wrong attempts: 3x17 input split by separator columns 5 and 11 (color 1) into three 3x5 panels; left pattern [[0,0,6,6,0],[8,0,6,0,0],[0,0,0,0,0]] was copied identically into the middle and right panels, retaining both separator columns. Do not alter separator cells or shift/reflect the template.\n\nAdditional confirmed test (task-9c09985c, 0-based indices): a 5x26 grid with separator columns 8 and 17 (color 3) formed three 5x8 panels. The middle panel was the only populated one; its exact rows were [[7,7,7,4,8,8,4,7],[7,5,7,7,7,2,1,1],[7,7,4,7,7,7,7,7],[7,7,1,7,0,6,0,7],[7,7,4,7,7,7,9,7]]. Copy this 5x8 panel identically into both outer panels, retaining both separator columns; accepted. Index carefully: row 1 middle panel ends in two 1s (values [7,5,7,7,7,2,1,1]), not a trailing 7. Initial wrong attempt came from misreading that row and was corrected by faithfully extracting all 8 cells from columns 9-16.", path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T03:49:11.931297+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T03:51:07.652710+00:00', version=4)
